clue.text: Wild cat, lithe and muscular

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of the two words run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild cat described as lithe and muscular, like a nature documentary caption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild cat' reads as one animal, but 'Wild' is the anagram signal working on CAT and LITHE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty and strongly built is described as athletic, a close synonym for brawny.

clue.text: Up to tree rocks taper off

indicators.note: to rock is to shake or disturb, so these letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Something climbing a tree in rocky ground narrows as it goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun of the landscape but is the verb that rearranges UP TO TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle gradually to nothing is to peter out, an idiom meaning to taper off or fade.

clue.text: Instruct male in type of wrestling close to Greco-Roman

indicators.note: the letter for male sits in the middle of the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so the end of Greco-Roman is taken

explanation.surface: Coaching a man in a wrestling style that resembles the Greco-Roman kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'similar to' but picks the last letter, N, of Greco-Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon is to call or order someone to come, so it can mean to instruct or command.

clue.text: Large cask on brewer's cart, last of many to be ditched in wasteland

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it, so the cask goes first

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for beer or wine

indicators.note: ditching something means throwing it away, so a letter is removed from the cart word

parts.note: a dray is the low cart brewers used to deliver barrels

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of many

explanation.surface: A barrel on a brewery cart, the last of many, is dumped in waste ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of many' gives Y, which is ditched from DRAY to leave DRA. A tun is a big cask; a dray is a brewer's cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless Arctic plain, a frozen wasteland.

clue.text: Greek tucked into a tuna I cooked, covered in breadcrumbs

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside the other, like a filling
cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek diner tucks into a cooked tuna dish topped with breadcrumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters into AUATIN, and 'tucked into' puts the Greek abbreviation inside, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish finished with a browned crust of breadcrumbs or grated cheese.

clue.text: Effective restraint in German plane

indicators.note: the restraint is placed inside the abbreviation for German

parts.note: to put a lid on something is to curb it effectively, so a lid is a restraint

explanation.surface: A German aircraft with an efficient restraining device.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft, a kind of plane that flies on air currents.

clue.text: Pictorial representation of Greek character keeping fit

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one word is held within the other

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
fit as in capable, able to do something

explanation.surface: A picture of a Greek figure staying in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person but is the letter TAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque group or scene, especially one posed silently on stage.

clue.text: Move most of allocated funds

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a budget is money set aside for a purpose

explanation.surface: A proposal to shift most of the money that has been set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position slightly, a synonym of move.

clue.text: In the customary manner, almost everyone gets behind a small American university

indicators.note: getting behind something means following it, so this piece comes last

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
US abbreviates American, as in United States

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone backing a little American college, as always.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from the word for everyone, and 'gets behind' places that piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: As usual is an everyday phrase meaning in the normal or habitual way.

clue.text: Opposed to increases in a toll, initially

parts.note: gains are increases or rises

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word toll

explanation.surface: Someone protesting against the rises in a road toll.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being opposed to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Daughter filling box in porter's room

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so this letter goes within the box word

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre

explanation.surface: A daughter packing a box in the doorkeeper's room.
explanation.walkthrough: A loge is a private box at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is the small house or room by a gate or entrance where a porter sits.

clue.text: Arm needed to be treated for wound

indicators.note: treating something processes or works on it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An injured arm needs treatment for its wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind (rhymes with 'found'), as a twisting path does.
explanation.definitionFit: A river or road that wound its way followed a twisting course, which is what meandered means.

clue.text: Get her informant drunk — when will he pay for it?

definitions.text: when will he pay for it?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting her informer drunk, and wondering when the price will be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic question: a drinker pays for the night's excess the next day, with a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: The next day after heavy drinking brings the hangover, so that is when the drunk informant suffers for it.

clue.text: Victoria, for example, punishable by death

definitions.meaning: Victoria is the chief city of British Columbia and of the Seychelles, a seat of government
a crime carrying the death penalty is described this way, as in such an offence

explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is the seat of government of the Seychelles, and a crime meriting execution is a capital offence.

clue.text: Dispensary quick to bandage injury

indicators.note: a bandage wraps round a wound, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: pacy means fast, quick
harm is injury or damage

explanation.surface: A clinic that is fast at dressing a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bandage' wraps the word for quick around the injury, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a shop where medicines are prepared and dispensed, so it is a dispensary.

clue.text: Writer upset, taken in by fat cat

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A writer is distressed and duped by a rich, smug feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' looks like one phrase but 'fat' is LARD and 'cat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a big spotted wild cat of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Coach's sports shoe

definitions.meaning: a coach is someone who trains athletes or teams
a soft shoe worn for running or sport

explanation.surface: A sports coach's running shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who coaches athletes is one sense; the other is a running shoe, a British term for a sneaker.

clue.text: One who's lost faith in a petty officer, say

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A sailor of rank who has lost his religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who renounces a religious belief, so one who has abandoned faith.

clue.text: Study, taking in facts about European rat

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the reversed piece goes inside the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: gen is informal British for information or facts

explanation.surface: A study that includes facts about a European rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the slang for facts, 'taking in' puts it inside the study word, and the European abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in the figurative sense is a deserter or traitor, which is what a renegade is.

clue.text: Snakebite: a possible answer to this question in pub!

definitions.text: Snakebite: a possible answer to this question in pub!

parts.words: Snakebite: a possible answer to this question in pub!
parts.note: snakebite is a drink of lager and cider, so it answers a barman's jokey question about what you drink; poison links to snakes

explanation.walkthrough: Snakebite suggests venom, but it is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the barman's jocular way of asking what drink you would like, and snakebite is one reply.

clue.text: Western county in former kingdom

parts.note: Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: A county in the west of England that was once a kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSEX is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in southern England, ruled by Alfred the Great.

clue.text: Pay tribute to late US comic

indicators.note: comic suggests something funny or absurd, so these letters are rearranged playfully

explanation.surface: Honouring a recently deceased American comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like a noun, the comedian, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour or praise them publicly, a synonym for paying tribute.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman can in the course of fund-raising event

indicators.note: something in the course of another happens within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity fund-raising event
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A sailor is allowed to take part during a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a TIN. A rag is a British student charity event.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the navy, an enlisted man rather than an officer.

clue.text: Impish youngster having nearly all of shellfish

indicators.note: nearly all means everything except the last letter

parts.note: scampi are langoustines, a shellfish dish

explanation.surface: A mischievous child eats most of the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous child, a rascal.

clue.text: Put out last, music programme on TV and radio at the same time?

definitions.text: programme on TV and radio at the same time?

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Broadcasting a music show at the end, on television and radio at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'broadcast', but it rearranges LAST and MUSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulcast is a broadcast transmitted simultaneously on radio and television.

clue.text: Regional intonation: trace once whiskey imbibed!

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the letter is taken inside the other word

parts.note: a tang is a trace or hint of flavour
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A local accent picks up a hint once some whiskey has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: W is whiskey from the NATO radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal accent characteristic of a region.

clue.text: Thrilled, left the stage carrying foremost of cups

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the word contains the letter

parts.note: exited is the stage direction for leaving

indicators.note: foremost is first, so the first letter of cups

explanation.surface: An actor, thrilled, leaves the stage holding trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means eager and stirred up, which is a synonym of thrilled.

clue.text: Do neat changes across page in jotter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across the letter, so it ends up inside them
changes means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Neat changes made across a page in a notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges DO NEAT into NOTEAD; 'across' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper for jotting notes, and a jotter is the same small notebook.
